data.title: What investors need to know about America's fastest-growing coffee chain
data.description:
Drive-thru coffee chain 7 Brew is one of the most intriguing stories in the retail sector. The Arkansas-based company is growing rapidly and has a cult-like following thanks to its stripped-down menu, fast service, and energetic baristas. That recipe has put pressure on established coffee chains such as Starbucks , Dutch Bros , Dunkin', Scooter's Coffee, and Black Rock Coffee Bar , as well as convenience-store operators in some markets.

The chain grew from 24 stores at the start of 2023 to 604 at the start of 2026 and now has more than 800, having opened 62 stands across 26 states in August alone. It is on track to surpass 1,000 locations by year-end. Earlier this year, 7 Brew launched a mobile app, began selling canned coffee at Walmart , and announced its first college-campus stand.

Almost all the growth comes from franchisees rather than company-owned stores. The company's 2026 plan calls for 437 franchise openings and about 10 corporate openings, with large, well-funded franchise groups driving much of the expansion. Investors such as Blackstone are backing the growth. The business model centers on small, low-cost drive-thru or walk-up stands with no seating. These locations are primarily in suburban areas and smaller markets with limited coffee competition, and they serve sweet, highly customizable drinks.

For investors, Blackstone's backing has fueled speculation about a potential 7 Brew IPO. The list of companies that went public while Blackstone was an investor includes Pinnacle Foods , SeaWorld Entertainment , Catalent, and Invitation Homes .

data.title: Central Bank of India Q2 net profit jumps 21% to ₹1,469 cr on higher core income
data.description:
Central Bank of India on Saturday reported a 21 per cent rise in net profit to ₹1,469 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, helped by improved core income and reduction in bad assets.

The public sector lender posted a net profit of ₹1,324 crore in the same period of the previous fiscal.

The bank's total income increased to ₹11,737 crore in the second quarter from ₹10,212 crore a year ago, Central Bank of India said in a regulatory filing.

Interest income rose to ₹10,357 crore in the September quarter of FY27 from ₹8,743 crore in the year-ago period.

During the quarter, net interest income rose 26 per cent to ₹4,146 crore against ₹3,283 crore in the second quarter of last financial year.

Cost-to-income ratio reduced to 58.95 per cent compared to 62.42 per cent in the year-ago period.

The bank's operating profit also increased to ₹2,268 crore from ₹2,186 crore a year ago.

As regards asset quality, gross non-performing assets (NPAs) of the bank moderated to 2.39 per cent of gross advances at the end of September 2026 compared to 3.01 per cent a year ago.

Similarly, net NPAs or bad loans came down to 0.31 per cent at the end of September 2026 against 0.48 per cent a year ago.

However, provisioning increased to ₹490 crore during the quarter against ₹144 crore in the July-September period of the last fiscal.

The Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) stood at 97.16 per cent as on September 30, 2026, registering a growth of 28 bps, from 96.88 per cent at the end of September 2025.

The Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) improved to 17.68 per cent from 17.48 per cent at the end of the second quarter of the previous financial year.

data.title: Reliance Consumer Director, Blinkit officials among 10 booked in expired-food probe
data.description:
Police in Bhiwandi, Maharashtra’s Thane district, have registered an FIR against a Reliance Consumer Products director and nine others, including officials associated with Reliance Retail, Blinkit and Hyperpure, following a Food and Drug Administration (FDA) investigation into the alleged diversion of expired and rejected food products back into retail markets. The regulator seized stock worth ₹48.09 lakh during inspections across Thane and Pune districts on October 14–15 and suspended licences of five facilities linked to the companies, senior FDA officials told businessline.

The investigation centres on whether warehouse operators and disposal contractors failed to ensure that expired, damaged and customer-rejected food products were destroyed. Instead, the goods were allegedly diverted through unlicensed sorting yards, brokers and retailers before reaching consumers, the officials said.

The FIR, registered at Shanti Nagar police station, names V. Subramaniam, whole-time director of Reliance Consumer Products, alongside officials associated with Reliance Retail, Blinkit and Eternal’s business-to-business food-supplies arm Hyperpure. Others named include a disposal-agency operator, local suppliers and a discount-store owner. The case invokes provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Five warehouse licences suspended

Seven FDA teams conducted coordinated inspections across Thane and Pune districts. Following hearings on October 15, the regulator suspended licences of Reliance Consumer Products and Reliance Retail facilities at Vadpe in Bhiwandi, a Reliance Retail warehouse at Chakan, Hyperpure’s Usatane facility and a Blinkit warehouse at Nighoje. The suspensions are facility-specific rather than company-wide.

The largest reported seizure, worth over ₹24 lakh, came from a Bhiwandi disposal yard. Officials also seized approximately ₹4.92 lakh of stock at Reliance Consumer Products’ Vadpe warehouse and ₹7.81 lakh at Hyperpure’s Usatane facility.

According to FDA officials, disposal agencies allegedly issued destruction certificates without adequately verifying that rejected goods had actually been destroyed. At unlicensed sorting yards, packets appearing saleable were separated and supplied to brokers and retailers. Expired and leaking products were subsequently found displayed for sale at an unlicensed Bhiwandi outlet.

Investigators also found alleged quantity mismatches and inconsistent consignor-consignee details in disposal records, raising questions about oversight of third-party contractors.

The case follows earlier FDA action against Amazon Retail India’s Bhiwandi warehouse over similar allegations. Its licence was suspended in June and subsequently cancelled. Amazon challenged the action in the Bombay High Court, which questioned the regulator’s approach and later ordered an interim arrangement for scientific disposal of expired stock.

Investigators must now establish whether warehouse operators verified actual destruction of rejected stock and determine responsibility across the disposal chain. The allegations remain under investigation.

data.title: DLF acquires 7.5 acres in Gurugram to expand luxury housing project
data.description:
DLF Ltd has acquired a 7.5-acre land in Gurugram to build a housing project as part of its expansion plan amid strong demand for luxury homes.

This plot is contiguous to 28 acres on Golf Course Extension Road that the company acquired in early 2024 from IREO, after taking over bad loans worth Rs 825 crore related to the land.

“We entered into a collaboration for a fresh 7.48 acres of land, which is contiguous to the 28 acres. So, eventually, it will be a 36-acre land parcel contiguous in Sector 61 (Gurugram) that we will have,” Managing Director Ashok Tyagi told analysts in a conference call on Saturday.

He said the company has made small payments to lenders in the September quarter towards this additional land parcel.

According to an investor presentation, DLF invested Rs 353 crore in the September quarter on payments related to land acquisition. In the first quarter of this fiscal, it had spent Rs 210 crore.

Tyagi said the land deal is expected to be completed by March end, but did not disclose the total land cost.

He also did not tell the timeline for launch of the housing project on this contiguous 36-acre plot.

Earlier acquisition involved ₹825-crore loan

According to a regulatory filing in 2024, DLF had entered into an agreement with Standard Chartered Bank, Singapore Branch, DB International (Asia), Singapore and Deutsche Investments India (lender/bond holder).

From these lenders, DLF agreed to buy non-convertible, redeemable bonds issued by IREO (bond issuer).

“Rs 825 crore was the outstanding loan that the developer had with these two banks. Actually, the loan was about Rs 1,200 crore. The bankers agreed to take a hair cut as a one-time settlement. So, Rs 825 crore is what we have bought the loan at from the bankers,” Tyagi had said in 2024.

Development potential to increase

The total development potential for the initial 28-acre plot is 7.5 million square ft, which will now increase significantly.

The Golf Course Extension Road has become an important micro market in the Gurugram residential market, with many leading developers launching luxury projects in this area.

DLF’s real estate portfolio

India’s largest realty firm DLF Ltd has developed more than 185 real estate projects so far, covering more than 352 million square feet of area.

The group has 275 million sq ft of development potential across residential and commercial segments, including current projects under execution.

data.title: YES Bank reports quarterly profit but flags impact of Supreme Court ruling on AT-1 bonds
data.description:
Yes Bank on Saturday reported a 65 per cent year-on-year jump in second-quarter profit to ₹1,080 crore ($114 million), but said the figure did not reflect the impact of a Supreme Court ruling this week that set aside its 2020 write-off of ₹8,400 crore ($884 million) in additional tier-1 bonds.

Had the impact been recognised, the bank would have posted a quarterly loss of ₹5,217 crore, it said in a filing.

data.title: ICICI Bank Q2 profit jumps 20.1% to ₹14,843 crore; margins come under pressure
data.description:
ICICI Bank reported a 20.1 per cent year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹14,843 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by strong growth in net interest income (NII). The bank posted a profit after tax (PAT) of ₹12,359 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year. However, PAT remained largely flat sequentially.

Net interest income rises 17.7 per cent

The bank’s net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest paid, rose 17.7 per cent to ₹R25,338.7 crore during the reporting quarter, compared with ₹21,529.5 crore a year earlier. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, NII increased 3.9 per cent to ₹24,384.4 crore.

Loan book expands 30 per cent

ICICI Bank’s loan book expanded 30 per cent year-on-year to ₹18.3 lakh crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with ₹14.08 lakh crore in the same period last year. Advances grew 12 per cent sequentially. Excluding the leverage provided on FCNR(B) loans, the bank’s lending grew 24.1 per cent year-on-year and 7.3 per cent quarter-on-quarter.

Deposits grow on FCNR(B) inflows

Deposits rose 27.1 per cent to ₹2.04 lakh crore in the quarter under review, up from ₹1.6 lakh crore in the year-ago period. Sequentially, deposits rose 11.8 per cent to ₹1.8 lakh crore from ₹ 1.6 lakh crore in the previous quarter.

FCNR(B) inflows contributed significantly to deposit growth. Excluding these NRI inflows, total deposits grew 17 per cent year-on-year and 3.1 per cent quarter-on-quarter as of September 30, 2026.

Net interest margin contracts

Despite strong profitability and business growth, the bank’s margins came under pressure. Net interest margin (NIM) fell to 4.18 per cent in the reporting quarter, down from 4.30 per cent in the year-ago period, a contraction of 12 basis points. The Q2 NIM was also 18 basis points lower than the 4.36 per cent recorded in the previous quarter. Excluding the benefit of interest income from a tax refund, the bank’s NIM stood at 4.28 per cent in the preceding quarter. On this adjusted basis, NIM fell by about 10 basis points in Q2.

Addressing the margin contraction, ICICI Bank Executive Director Sandeep Batra said the decline was largely attributable to the cost of FCNR(B) inflows. “Talking of the decline from 4.28 per cent to 4.18 per cent, it is largely a function of FCNR(B), which results in a higher deposit base and a lower CASA ratio,” Batra said during the media call.

data.title: Axis Bank Q2 profit rises 37.6% to ₹7,003 crore as provisions fall 52.2%
data.description:
Axis Bank reported a 37.6 per cent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to ₹7,003 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, driven by strong core income growth, robust loan book expansion, and a sharp decline in provisioning costs. The lender had posted a net profit of ₹5,090 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Sequentially, profit eased marginally by 1.6 per cent to ₹7,114 crore from ₹7,214 crore in Q1 FY27.

Net interest income rises 12 per cent

The bank’s net interest income (NII) grew 12 per cent year-on-year to ₹15,371 crore from ₹13,745 crore in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, NII grew around 5 per cent, supported by strong momentum across retail, SME and wholesale banking businesses. Net interest margin (NIM) stood at 3.36 per cent during the quarter and 3.47 per cent excluding the impact of FCNR(B) deposits, reflecting margin resilience amid a competitive funding environment.

Advances grow across retail, SME and wholesale businesses

The strong earnings growth was underpinned by healthy loan growth across businesses. Total advances grew 23 per cent year-on-year and 9 per cent quarter-on-quarter, while advances excluding loans linked to FCNR(B) deposits increased 19 per cent year-on-year. Retail advances expanded 16 per cent year-on-year, driven by healthy disbursement trends across products. The SME portfolio continued to outperform, growing 25 per cent year-on-year, supported by differentiated offerings and technology-led capabilities, while the wholesale banking franchise grew 34 per cent year-on-year on robust client activity and deeper relationship-led engagement.

Lower provisions boost profitability

Operating profit stood at ₹11,083 crore, up 6.4 per cent year-on-year but down 4.9 per cent sequentially from ₹11,659 crore in the June quarter, as operating expenses rose faster than revenue. Operating expenses increased to ₹10,819 crore from ₹9,722 crore in the preceding quarter, led by higher employee expenses and other operating costs. Employee costs rose to ₹3,314 crore from ₹3,058 crore. Lower provisioning drove profit growth during the quarter. Provisions and contingencies fell 52.2 per cent year-on-year to ₹1,694 crore from ₹3,547 crore, helping profit before tax rise 36.8 per cent to ₹9,389 crore.

Management highlights growth and risk discipline

“Growth was achieved through higher wallet share from existing customers while maintaining disciplined risk thresholds,” said Amitabh Chaudhry, MD & CEO of Axis Bank. “We delivered robust growth in deposits and advances, supported by strong NII growth, improving asset quality and healthy operating performance, while maintaining strong liquidity and capital buffers to support future growth,” said Rajeev Mantri, Group CFO, Axis Bank.

Deposits grow as asset quality improves

On the liability side, total deposits grew 23 per cent year-on-year, supported by strong growth in term deposits, CASA balances, and FCNR(B) inflows. Asset quality remained a key positive, with the gross NPA ratio improving to 1.16 per cent from 1.46 per cent a year ago and the net NPA ratio declining to 0.35 per cent from 0.44 per cent. Net credit cost reduced to 0.45 per cent, reflecting lower stress formation and prudent risk management. Improved asset quality, along with strong operating performance, was a major contributor to the sharp rise in profits during the quarter.

Rahul Shukla appointed Group Head

Separately, the bank appointed Rahul Shukla as Group Head, Commercial and Bharat Banking, effective October 19, 2026, strengthening its senior management team.

data.title: HDFC Bank veteran Kaizad Bharucha quits
data.description:
In a major shake-up at HDFC Bank, its Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha has decided to quit, after being passed over for appointment as Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer  of India’s largest private sector bank.

This comes about a fortnight after RBI approved the Bank’s application for appointment of Anup Bagchi (former Chief of ICICI Life Insurance, who joined HDFC Bank’s board as an Additional Director with effect from October 2, 2026) as its MD & CEO for three years with effect from October 27, 2026.

Bharucha is HDFC Bank’s longest serving board member, having joined it in 2014. He was re-appointed Whole-time Director/WTD (Deputy Managing Director) of the Bank for three years with effect from April 19, 2026.

Late August 2026, Sashidhar Jagdishan decided not to seek re-appointment as the MD&CEO  of HDFC Bank for a third term amid controversy that started with the abrupt resignation of the Bank’s Part-Time Chairman in March 2026. His term ends on October 26, 2026.

The Bank on Saturday informed the exchanges that Bharucha has requested cessation from the service of the Bank with effect from the close of business hours on December 31, 2026.

“The GNRC (Governance, Nomination and Remuneration Committee) and the Board of Directors, at their respective meetings held on October 16, 2026 and October 17, 2026, respected the decision of Bharucha and accepted his request to be forwarded to the RBI for approval,” per the Bank’s filing.

With two veterans — Sashidhar and Bharucha -moving on, HDFC Bank will have two new WTDs — Bagchi and a new candidate, who could either be an insider or an outsider.

In September 2026, the Bank sought RBI’s approval for appointment of Jimmy Tata (currently Chief Credit Offocer) as a WTD designated as Executive Director) of the Bank for three years.

In a media concall, Jagdishan emphasised that HDFC Bank has been driven more by processes and not by an individual personality. Further, the depth in management is so large that the continuity and the ethos of the institution will be intact as well.

‘So Anup comes in and he will lead a team of able leaders who have been with the institution for a long time…and they will be the fulcrum (of the organisation) and ably support Anup to chart out his vision and his strategy as well. So, you know, he has about 34 years of experience in the field of financial services,” said Jagdishan, adding that “ he is a seasoned player who has been not just in banking, but also in insurance. So he has a very holistic view….So I wish him the very best, and you will hear more from him going forward.”

Bagchi, who joined the call, said: “I’m going to engage with all — the regulators, customers, stakeholders, and gather insights, and that will become a key input to our operational priorities.  And if you look at the leadership, they have spent many, many years within this system. And they know the system, they are fully committed to the institution. So, in fact, I’m very, very lucky to be a part of an institution which is solid, very sound.”

data.title: Punjab & Sind Bank records 40% rise in net profit in Q2
data.description:
With improvement in interest earning, Punjab & Sind Bank on Saturday reported a net profit of ₹412 crore during July-September quarter of FY 27. This is 40 per cent higher than ₹295 crore achieved during corresponding period of last fiscal.

The bank’s net interest income stood at ₹1,162 crore for the quarter, showing a growth of over 22 per cent. Net Interest Margin improved by 17 bps to 2.77 per cent. During the quarter, provisions and contingencies dropped sharply, giving a boost to the net profit. Gross non-performing assets improved to 2.09 per cent from 2.92 per cent a year earlier and 2.21 per cent in the previous quarter (QoQ). Net NPAs declined to 0.61 per cent from 0.83 per cent

data.title: FSSAI issues notices to Nestle, HUL for misleading claims
data.description:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India on Saturday said that it has issued notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever regarding misleading claims and non-compliances with regards to certain products. It has also suspended licences of Sukhdarshan Pharma and Bala Ji Food Products for serious food safety violations. This comes as recent inspections and audits have led to strict enforcement actions against several major brand manufacturers and local FBOs for misleading claims, non-compliance with labelling regulations, and severe food safety violations.

The food safety regulator said that Nestle India was found marketing and selling “Nescafé Intense Café” Cappuccino flavour, “Nescafé Choco Mocha” and “Nescafé Chilled Latte” on e-commerce platforms with “inconsistent descriptions on the packaging.”

The products, manufactured by Schreiber Dynamix Dairies and Lotus Dairy Products were found to be making the declaration of “Flavoured Milk” in the front of the pack while the back of the pack declares, ““Proprietary Food – 1.12 Dairy Based Drink.”

It added that the e-commerce listings also described the products as “Coffee Flavoured Milk”,resulting in inconsistency between the product label and its advertisements. “

It also noted that the product descriptions on e-commerce platforms were found to contain claims such as “crafted with the goodness of flavoured double toned milk”, which are not consistent with the declared composition and category of the product. It added that since the products fall under the category of “Flavoured Milks”, the company’s declaration as proprietary food was found to be “incorrect.” “Such inconsistent labelling, product descriptions and advertisements were found to be in contravention of the applicable provision of the FSS (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018 and FSS (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020,” it said.

Misleading claims

In a separate notice issued to Nestle India, the FSSAI has flagged misleading claims on the company’s “renal resource vanilla flavour powder.” It said that the examination of the product label, ad and product listing on the e-commerce platform revealed non-compliances. It noted that the product is intended for a special medical condition and requires prior approval of the FSSAI, which has not been obtained by the company rendering it non-compliant.

The food safety regulator has also issued two notices to Hindustan Unilever for Horlicks Women’s Plus Chocolate Nutrition Drink and Horlicks Mother’s Plus Kesar for misleading claims. FSSAI has flagged claims such as “nutrition for strong bones” and “clinically proven to help improve bone strength” as “misleading or non-compliant” with regulations.

It noted that use of the term “healthy” in food claims found to be on Horlicks’ Women Plus is in contravention with the regulations. Nutritional Information was also not provided in the prescribed form. Also the claim of “100 per cent RDA of Calcium, Vitamin D & K2” was found not to comply with food safety requirements. In the case of Horlicks Mother’s Plus Kesar, FSSAI has flagged claims such as “Healthy Birth Weight” on the product label and “For baby’s healthy birth weight” in the advertisement as potentially misleading and in contravention of the FSS (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.

The food safety regulator also said it has suspended the licence of Sukhdarshan Pharma for serious food safety, hygiene and sanitation violations. Meanwhile, the regulator has also suspended the license of Bala Ji Food Products due to serious food safety violation and continued non-compliance with applicable food safety requirements.

data.title: Kenya confirms four new Ebola cases, bringing total number to seven
data.description:
Kenya confirmed four new cases of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus on Saturday, including three health workers who treated the country's first patient, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to seven, the health ministry said.

The other new case is a male relative of the index patient, who died. The relative had been in quarantine since October 6, the ministry said in a statement.

The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya, where the first patient arrived from Congo on October 3. But the ministry says it has traced and quarantined nearly all of his contacts and there is no evidence that the virus is spreading in the community.

The three health workers — two men and a woman aged 29, 35 and 32 respectively — managed the index case on October 3 and 4 and had been in quarantine since October 9, it said. All four new patients were already in quarantine when they developed symptoms and were diagnosed.

The second and third patients confirmed earlier are stable and responding well to supportive treatment, the ministry said. It said 128 of 130 listed contacts, or 98.5%, had been traced and placed in quarantine, higher than the 85% global benchmark it said was needed to break the chain of transmission.

Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo — the second-largest outbreak ever recorded, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths.

There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola.

The first Kenyan case was a man who had been ill in Congo for about a month before travelling by road to Uganda and flying to Nairobi on October 3. He died on October 5. His arrival has raised concerns about screening at the Congo-Uganda border, which has been closed since May, and at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.

Efforts to trace the remaining two contacts were ongoing, the ministry said. "The risk to the general public remains low as there is no evidence of community transmission," it said, adding that there were no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings.

data.title: FSSAI initiates prosecution against Surya Food & Agro for using cattle feed bran in Priyagold biscuits production
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has initiated legal proceedings for prosecution against Surya Food & Agro, the manufacturer of Priyagold biscuits, for allegedly using cattle feed bran in biscuit production and violating food safety requirements.

The regulator has also initiated prosecution proceedings against Dodla Dairy and UEIR Organic Foods over food safety violations involving substandard full cream milk and pesticide residues in yellow raisins, respectively.

The FSSAI said that it has "initiated legal proceedings for prosecution" against these three companies for "serious food safety violations".

The actions follow regulatory inspections and laboratory analysis that identified non-compliance with food safety standards. The proceedings have been initiated under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

FSSAI inspected Surya Food & Agro following a consumer complaint and found serious deficiencies related to food safety, hygiene and manufacturing practices.

During the inspection, the regulator found that the company was using bran intended for cattle feed in the manufacture of Priyagold biscuits. The gunny bags containing the material were marked to indicate that it was meant for cattle consumption.

The inspection also identified shortcomings in several areas, including plant hygiene, pest control, raw material storage and segregation, personnel hygiene, maintenance of the premises and handling of intermediate formulations.

"Bran meant for cattle feed and not intended for human consumption, was found being used as a raw material in Priyagold biscuit manufacturing as a source of fibre," the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said in a social media post on Saturday.

These findings raised concerns about the company's compliance with prescribed food safety and hygiene requirements.

FSSAI had earlier suspended Surya Food & Agro's licence following serious non-compliances detected during the inspection. The regulator has now initiated legal proceedings for prosecution against the company over the violations.

FSSAI has also initiated prosecution proceedings against Dodla Dairy after a regulatory sample of its full cream milk was declared substandard.

The sample was collected by the food safety authorities and sent for laboratory analysis. The Food Analyst found that the milk did not conform to the prescribed specifications for milk fat.

Upon appeal by the company, the sample was referred to the Referral Food Laboratory, which "confirmed that the sample was unsafe due to the presence of detergent/caustic soda and substandard due to milk fat below the minimum prescribed limit."

The laboratory findings established violations relating to substandard food under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

Following the analysis, the competent authority granted sanction for initiating prosecution against Dodla Dairy and other concerned food business operators associated with the manufacture and marketing of the product.

The authorities have directed further prosecution proceedings in connection with the substandard food findings.

In a separate case, FSSAI initiated legal proceedings for prosecution against UEIR Organic Foods after pesticide residues were detected in a sample of yellow raisins sold by the company.

The finding raised food safety concerns and prompted regulatory action against the business.

The cases involving Surya Food & Agro, Dodla Dairy and UEIR Organic Foods highlight separate instances of alleged non-compliance with food safety requirements, ranging from the use of an ingredient designated for animal feed to milk quality deficiencies and pesticide contamination.

The prosecution proceedings mark a further step in the regulator's response to the violations identified through consumer complaints, inspections and laboratory testing. The cases will proceed through the applicable legal process under food safety regulations.

data.title: Grayscale Opens DeFi And AI Crypto Funds To Investors With Just $2,500
data.description:
TL;DR: Grayscale and investment platform Republic are offering three specialised crypto funds with minimum commitments starting at $2,500. The products remain restricted to eligible accredited investors.

Grayscale is opening another route into sector-specific cryptocurrency investing, reducing the minimum commitment for selected private funds through a distribution partnership with Republic.

The products focus on decentralised finance, artificial intelligence and blockchain data infrastructure. Eligible investors can gain exposure through managed vehicles rather than purchasing every underlying cryptocurrency themselves.

The $2,500 entry level is significantly lower than the sums typically associated with institutional private placements, but the offering should not be mistaken for a mass-market retail investment product.

Beyond Bitcoin And Ethereum

Grayscale’s decentralised finance portfolio includes projects associated with lending, trading and other blockchain-based financial services. Its AI strategy covers networks involved in decentralised computing and related technology.

The partnership illustrates how asset managers are packaging more specialised cryptocurrency themes for investors who already understand conventional investment products.

Grayscale has separately explored staking-related changes to its Ethereum and Solana investment structures, reflecting its effort to develop products beyond straightforward token-price exposure.

The Important Restrictions

Participation in the Republic offering is limited to accredited investors under applicable US securities rules. Private investment products may impose selling restrictions, and their holdings can be considerably less liquid than publicly traded ETFs.

The lower minimum also does nothing to eliminate the volatility of the cryptocurrencies inside each portfolio.

Still, the arrangement provides another example of how traditional asset managers are attempting to make a wider variety of digital assets accessible through familiar investment structures.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Yes Bank Q2 profit rises but AT1 ruling not booked as further appeal weighed
data.description:
By Ashwin Manikandan

Yes Bank on Saturday reported a 65% jump in second-quarter profit to 10.80 billion Indian rupees ($114 million), but said the figure does not reflect the impact of a Supreme Court ruling this week that set aside its 2020 write-off of 84 billion rupees ($884 million) of additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds.

Had the impact been recognised, the bank would have posted a quarterly loss of 52.17 billion rupees, it said in a filing.

The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a 2023 Bombay High Court judgment that set aside the write-down, dismissing appeals by the lender, the Reserve Bank of India and the federal government.

The Mumbai-based lender, in which Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation [RIC:RIC:SUMFDS.UL] holds a 24.99% stake, said it was evaluating the implications, including the manner and timing of implementation.

It is also weighing "all legal remedies available", including further proceedings before the Supreme Court.

The figures are indicative and subject to revision, the bank said.

If they were adjusted to reflect the court ruling, the bank's net worth would fall to 469.70 billion rupees from 532.68 billion, and borrowings would rise to 861.49 billion rupees from 777.34 billion, it said.

Its total capital adequacy ratio would stay unaffected at 14.5%, the bank said. It had said in a filing on Friday that its common equity tier-1 ratio would decline about 250 basis points.

AT1 bonds are high-risk debt instruments that can be written off or converted into equity when a bank comes under financial stress.

Yes Bank, a mid-sized lender, was rescued in 2020 under a restructuring scheme that brought in new investors. The bonds were written off by an administrator in charge of the restructuring.

Analysts had forecast a profit of 9.55 billion rupees, according to LSEG data.

The bank's net interest income rose 22.7% to 28.22 billion rupees. Advances grew 23.7% from a year earlier and deposits rose 19.5%.

Provisions for bad loans and other contingencies fell 24.2% to 3.17 billion rupees. Other income rose 14.4% to 18.82 billion rupees.

The gross non-performing asset ratio was 1.2% at end-September, against 1.3% at end-June.

($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

data.title: Earnings Scorecard: 14 out of 18 financial companies beat EPS estimates this week
data.description:
Financial companies remained in the spotlight this week as investors digested quarterly results from the largest payment companies, insurers, exchanges, brokers, and asset managers.

Major names including JPMorgan Chase & Co. , Citigroup , Wells Fargo , Goldman Sachs , Bank of America , Morgan Stanley , and BlackRock reported earnings during the week.

The Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF gained 0.7% over the past week, compared with a 2% decline in the S&P 500 (SP500). On a YTD basis, XLF has underperformed the broader market with 0.8% returns, while the S&P 500 has gained nearly 12%.

Earnings Roundup

Top Line (Revenue): 11 companies beat revenue estimates, while seven missed.

Below are some of the key companies that reported earnings this week:

The U.S.'s largest bank by assets, JPMorgan Chase's Q3 earnings and revenue missed Wall Street consensus estimates. Its Q3 commercial and investment banking results softened markedly from Q2's robust pace. Each line of business, though, grew from the year-ago quarter.

Citigroup Q3 earnings exceeded the Wall Street consensus as its services and wealth units posted solid gains after markets and investment banking revenue weakened from the previous quarter. The lender now expects full-year 2026 net interest income, ex-markets, to rise in the mid-to-high 6% range from 2025’s $49.8B, compared with its prior guidance of ~5%-6%.

Wells Fargo capital market revenues fell short of expectations during the third quarter, impacting overall revenue at the San Francisco-based bank. For the fourth quarter, NII is expected to be ~$13B, vs. $12.82B consensus.

Goldman Sachs () Q3 top and bottom lines exceeded consensus estimates even as markets-related revenue eased from an unusually strong Q2. Solid growth in its asset and wealth management business helped to offset the less hectic market activity in Q3.

Bank of America reported Q3 diluted EPS of $0.91, down from $1.04 a year earlier and below the $1.09 consensus estimate. Results were impacted by a $1.2 billion U.S. Treasury fine for anti-money laundering and sanctions violations, which reduced EPS by $0.17.

BlackRock reported its Q3 results, beating Wall Street earnings and revenue expectations across the board.

Overall, financial sector earnings were resilient this week. About 78% of reported companies beat EPS estimates, while 61% beat revenue expectations, showing that many companies continued to deliver solid profits despite mixed revenue growth.

Earnings next week

For the upcoming week, investors will continue to watch earnings from the financial sector, such as American Express , Blackstone , Capital One Financial , and Synchrony Financial .

data.title: Brace Your Budget: Grocery Inflation Is Set to Accelerate — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Megan Leonhardt

The cost of groceries has been surprisingly stable in recent months, but don't expect that calm to last. Inflation is expected to climb again over the next year, with households and policymakers bearing the brunt.

Overall food inflation, as measured by the consumer price index, has been relatively stable in recent months, with flat monthly growth in September after a 0.1% advance in both July and August. Over the past 12 months, food inflation has only risen 2.5%, below the overall pace of 3.7% year over year headline inflation in September.

But that slower pace of rising food prices is set to end. Higher energy prices, particularly diesel costs, are feeding into transportation expenses even as elevated tariff rates have raised costs for many of the components in food packaging. Moreover, El Niño threatens to upend agricultural production in the Western U.S., Mexico, and South America in the coming months, which could limit supply and raise prices.

"There is a little slice of relief for food currently, and folks should enjoy it while it lasts because these higher energy costs and some other factors are going to filter in by the end of the year," says Ricky Volpe, a prominent professor of agribusiness at California Polytechnic State University in San Luis Obispo.

The U.S. is on track to see food inflation of 3.5% to 4% next year, Volpe tells Barron's. That's still far from the last bout of peak food inflation, which rose 11.4% year over year in August 2022.

"It's not runaway food price inflation, but food prices are continuing to go up at a time where I think people want them to go down," Volpe says. For context, U.S. food inflation has averaged approximately 2.8% annually over the past 30 years.

The higher expected food prices could squeeze household budgets, particularly for lower- and middle-income families already struggling with higher costs of living.

However, it likely won't significantly affect aggregate consumer spending levels — especially since much of the momentum has been fueled by wealthier households. Last year, the bulk of aggregate spending was done by the wealthiest families, with those in the top decile of wealth spending $136,000 on average, accounting for 27.9% of the total expenditures, according to the Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances. American families in the bottom quintile of wealth spent an average of just $23,400 in 2025.

But higher food costs are not something that the Federal Reserve can shrug off, especially if demand holds up. Economists generally look through short-term shocks to specific products, such as when a severe outbreaks of avian influenza sent egg prices soaring nationwide in early 2025. Broad-based food inflation, however, is another story.

Many Fed officials routinely cite core inflation, which excludes food and energy costs, because it has been shown to more accurately reflect price growth trends over time. However, the Fed's official 2% inflation target is based on the annual change in the overall personal consumption expenditures price index. That means food inflation cannot be dismissed.

The biggest threat to food prices in the coming months continues to be the ongoing energy shock. Brent crude oil futures hit a high of $110 a barrel this week, while West Texas Intermediate crude oil reached a high of $101 per barrel.

Persistently higher energy prices have certainly driven up consumer inflation, but they had an even bigger impact on producer prices in September. The producer price index, which tracks wholesale inflation, rose 1.3% on the month in September — the fastest pace in more than four years.

Within the producer price data, wholesale food costs were up 1.2% month over month, reversing three months of declines. Additionally, the September retail sales report also showed a rise in grocery spending, suggesting that Americans are spending more on necessities as prices climb.

"The producer price index for September showed clear evidence of rising wholesale prices in energy, transportation and food that will result in thinner producer margins and costs being passed downstream to American households," writes Joe Brusuelas, chief economist for RSM US LLP.

Higher diesel prices first hit farmers during the planting season and continued to plague the agricultural sector during the summer harvest, Brusuelas says. "Eventually, all eyes will be focused on agriculture and grocery prices, which are likely to rise because of the limited availability of fertilizers earlier this year and the recent jump in transportation prices," he adds.

The U.S. has not seen the full impact of those higher fuel prices yet, Volpe says. "The food system is energy-intense and most food companies operate on thin margins. So I'm a little surprised we haven't seen higher inflation yet, but we will. I think food price inflation has to accelerate," Volpe says.

Expect the passthrough of higher energy prices to hit highly perishable food categories first. Prices on fresh whole chickens, for example, rose 3.9% month over month in September, reversing two months of declining price growth. Similarly, prices for fresh fruits and vegetables were also up in September after two months of outright declines.

To gauge the broader scope of the potential inflation risk to food prices, Volpe is carefully watching where corn yields and prices end up this season. "It looks like we're having a strong yield, not as strong as last year, but nothing to worry about. But nevertheless, prices may end up being problematic, because this is the crop that was planted with the higher energy and fertilizer crop prices that came as the result of that initial outbreak of the conflict in Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz," Volpe says.

If it turns out that the U.S. has substantial increases for field corn prices grown throughout the U.S., that's going to filter into higher food prices for at least three to six months at the start of 2027, he says.

Tariffs are another, albeit less impactful inflationary pressure on food prices. Direct food tariffs have not had the impact that many initially feared. But there's an ongoing cost pressure that is worth considering and is likely starting to affect food prices, Volpe says. Tariffs remain in place for some of the key building blocks for the food supply chain, such as steel, aluminum, paper, and cardboard.

"That's not going to affect the food system overnight, because food companies have been working off of inventories and doing their best to make substitutions and relying on domestic supply. But that can't last forever," Volpe says.

El Niño, a weather phenomenon that typically results in wetter and cooler conditions in the Western and Southwest portions of the country, poses another threat to food prices. The current conditions are already tracking as one of the strongest El Niño events on record. If the rains start early or run late, that could result in a large swath of stunted growth, as well as higher instances of mold and crop affecting leafy greens, berries, grapes, and nuts.

"That's absolutely going to have an impact," Volpe says, but adds it's one the U.S. probably won't experience the effects from until mid-2027, given the timing of the planting and harvest cycles.

Already, there is mounting frustration nationwide over higher costs of living. For instance, the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index hit its second-lowest level ever in October. Rising food costs certainly won't help improve consumer pessimism — and could help spur Fed officials to further increase interest rates if the situation proves broad-based.

Write to Megan Leonhardt at megan.leonhardt@barrons.com

data.title: Ixigo Swings To Rs 63 Crore Profit In Q2
data.description:
Travel booking platform ixigo reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 63.42 crore for the September quarter, compared with a loss of Rs 3.46 crore a year earlier, helped by a partial stake sale in Freshbus and rapid growth in hotel bookings.

Revenue from operations rose 13 per cent year-on-year to Rs 320.96 crore in the second quarter of FY27, from Rs 284.23 crore in the corresponding period last year, according to a regulatory filing by Le Travenues Technology, which operates ixigo.

Total expenses increased to Rs 309.51 crore from Rs 291.89 crore a year earlier.

The company reported quarterly gross transaction value (GTV) of Rs 5,304 crore, up 22 per cent year-on-year, reflecting continued growth in its travel booking business.

Hotels was ixigo's fastest-growing business segment by GTV, with the metric rising 159 per cent year-on-year to Rs 111.34 crore. The September quarter marked the first time the company reported hotels as a separate business line.

In a joint statement, ixigo Group Chief Executive Officer Aloke Bajpai, Group Co-CEO Rajnish Kumar and Group Chief Financial Officer Saurabh Devendra Singh said the company had recorded its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax, aided by the partial sale of its stake in Freshbus.

The executives said the company would continue investing in hotels and artificial intelligence as key drivers of its long-term growth.

data.title: GPT Infraprojects Secures Rs 134 Cr Western Railway Signalling Contract
data.description:
The project covers four railway sections in Ratlam division, with completion scheduled within 548 days from the appointed date

GPT Infraprojects has secured a railway signalling contract worth Rs 134.11 crore, including GST, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Alcon Builders and Engineers Private Limited, the company said in a stock exchange filing.

The order has been awarded by the Chief Signal and Telecommunication Engineer, Western Railway, Ratlam Division, with the contract valued at Rs 113.65 crore excluding GST. The project covers signalling works across multiple double-line railway sections under the Ratlam division.

The scope includes survey, design, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of 4-Aspect Automatic Block Signalling with electronic interlocking and dual multi-section digital axle counters at auto huts. The contract also covers associated alterations to electronic interlocking systems at stations.

The works will be executed across the Nagda-Ujjain-Tajpur, Phanda-Sant Hirdaram Nagar, Ujjain-Karchha and Mangliyagaon-Indore double-line sections. GPT Infraprojects said the project is scheduled for completion within 548 days from the appointed date.

With the latest contract, GPT Infraprojects' net outstanding order book has reached Rs 5,651 crore. The company has recorded total order inflow of Rs 1,478 crore so far in fiscal 2027, strengthening its project pipeline for the year.

GPT Infraprojects operates through infrastructure and sleeper segments, with its infrastructure business covering civil and railway projects. Its activities include bridges, road-over-bridges and railway signalling works, alongside concrete sleeper manufacturing.

Railway Business Gains

The company manufactures concrete sleepers for railway projects through facilities in West Bengal, South Africa, Namibia and Ghana. Its operations therefore span both infrastructure execution and railway component manufacturing across India and overseas markets.

Shares of GPT Infraprojects ended nearly 1 per cent higher on the day. The stock has gained around 15 per cent so far this year, as the company continues to build its order pipeline across railway and infrastructure projects.

data.title: RailTel Secures Rs 186.5 Cr Orders For Recruitment, Cybersecurity
data.description:
The larger project runs through 2031 for railway recruitment services, while the second covers technology and cybersecurity support through 2029

RailTel Corporation of India has secured two work orders worth a combined Rs 186.51 crore, including a Rs 167.52 crore contract from the Railway Recruitment Board (RRB), Secunderabad, for recruitment examination services.

The company received both orders on 16 October, according to its regulatory filing. The contracts cover recruitment examination management as well as IT infrastructure and cybersecurity solutions, further adding to RailTel's project pipeline.

The larger order, estimated at Rs 167.52 crore excluding taxes, covers AM-RMS services for the pre-examination and post-examination stages of RRB recruitment conducted through various Centralised Employment Notifications (CENs).

The contract is scheduled to remain valid until 15 October 2031, giving RailTel a long-term engagement to provide services associated with the recruitment examination process conducted by the railway recruitment board.

IT Infrastructure Order

The second order, worth Rs 18.99 crore including taxes, has been awarded by Health Insurance TPA of India Ltd for IT infrastructure and cybersecurity solutions. The three-year contract is scheduled to run until 16 October 2029, expanding RailTel's recent project wins across technology, digital infrastructure and cybersecurity-related services.

The latest contracts follow several orders secured by RailTel in recent months, covering digital governance, telecom infrastructure and technology services for government and public-sector clients.

On 13 October, RailTel received a Rs 49 crore order, including taxes, from the Odisha government's Higher Education Department to develop 83 digital application modules under a Comprehensive Digital Governance Platform.

In August, the company secured a Rs 165 crore contract, including taxes, from Western Coalfields to establish a Multiprotocol Label Switching Virtual Private Network on a rental basis for 60 months.

The Western Coalfields contract is scheduled to continue until 20 September 2031. RailTel also received a Rs 166.8 crore order from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation in August to extend an existing Infrastructure-as-a-Service arrangement through RailTel by one year.

The EPFO contract includes additional components and is scheduled to run until 9 February 2027. RailTel shares closed at Rs 255.05 on the BSE on 16 October, rising 0.57 per cent during the session.

data.title: Nifty soars 2.8% this week: What lies ahead for Dalal Street? - Experts decode 5 triggers, key levels for next week
data.description:
Stock Market Outlook, Oct. 17 -- Indian equities staged a strong comeback this week, with the Nifty 50 rising 2.77% and the Sensex surging 3.11%, as renewed buying in information technology (IT) stocks, easing global bond-yield pressures and resilient domestic institutional inflows lifted investor sentiment.

Both benchmarks also extended their gains for a second consecutive session on Friday, strengthening hopes of a recovery after the recent market correction.

On Friday, the Sensex climbed 413.66 points, or 0.56%, to close at 74,729.27 on Friday, while the Nifty advanced 148.80 points, or 0.65%, to settle at 23,146.15. For the week, the Sensex gained 2,256.94 points, while the Nifty added 625.7 points.

However, the rally faces several tests, including whether earnings growth broadens beyond IT, foreign investor selling eases further and the Nifty breaks through immediate resistance. Market experts believe investors should remain selective as global macroeconomic uncertainty and domestic inflation concerns persist.

The September-quarter earnings season will remain a major driver of market sentiment. Investors will assess whether companies can deliver stronger revenue growth and margins across banking, consumption and industrials, rather than relying primarily on IT stocks to sustain the recovery.

Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments Limited, said, "The sustainability of the recovery will hinge on earnings growth broadening beyond IT, with revenue and margin delivery across financials, consumption and industrials under close scrutiny."

Foreign institutional investor (FII) flows remain a key variable for the market. While foreign portfolio outflows have moderated, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continue to provide support through sustained buying.

Ravi Singh, Chief Research Officer at Master Capital Services Ltd, said weekly foreign portfolio outflows narrowed to Rs.8,991 crore, while domestic institutional investors purchased approximately Rs.7,813 crore worth of shares. Any further moderation in foreign selling could help stabilise the indices.

Global monetary policy expectations, geopolitical developments and energy prices will remain important determinants of investor appetite for equities. Higher crude prices can fuel inflation, while rising bond yields may increase the relative attractiveness of fixed-income investments and put pressure on equity valuations.

Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research, Religare Broking. noted, "Global markets are currently in a transition phase. Major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, have started moving towards an easier monetary policy stance, while growth remains subdued across regions such as Europe and China."

IT shares have been a key driver of the recent recovery, supported by a shift in global investor positioning following a sell-off in international AI and semiconductor stocks. Singh attributed the buying interest in Indian IT services companies to concerns over elevated valuations and delayed monetisation cycles among global AI hardware and chipmakers.

Indian IT companies, with their established execution capabilities and comparatively attractive valuations, have benefited from this rotation. Investors will watch whether the momentum continues or broadens to other sectors.

The Nifty has rebounded from support near 22,200 and reclaimed its 21-day exponential moving average (EMA) around 22,900, indicating improving near-term momentum. However, the index must overcome immediate resistance to extend its recovery.

Singh said, "As long as Nifty sustains above this level, buying interest is likely to persist, making a buy-on-dips strategy prudent. On the upside, the 55-day EMA near 23360 remains the immediate resistance."

The near-term technical setup has improved, but experts favour selective stock picking over aggressive index-level positioning.

The Nifty's immediate resistance is around 23,360, corresponding to its 55-day EMA. A decisive breakout could open the way towards 23,600, according to Singh's technical assessment. On the downside, the 21-day EMA near 22,900 is an important level to defend, while 22,200 remains a significant support zone.

Mishra's medium-term assessment is constructive, subject to an improvement in corporate earnings. The analyst said, "Immediate resistance sits near 23,800-24,000; a sustained breakout above that could set up a retest of the 26,350-26,500 zone over 6 months, contingent on earnings acceleration."

The analyst identified 23,000 as immediate support, followed by the 52-week low near 22,182. These are medium-term levels and should be distinguished from the nearer-term technical markers highlighted by Singh.

For investors, a staggered buy-on-dips approach may be preferable to chasing sharp rallies, provided key support levels hold. Companies with sustainable earnings growth, strong balance sheets and reasonable valuations are likely to offer a more disciplined route through continued volatility.

India's October PMI, US jobless claims, Japan's inflation data, Corporate earnings and management commentary, rupee, crude oil bond yields, and FII and DII activity will be closely watched next week.

Nair cautioned that the market was likely to remain selective and earnings-driven amid elevated inflation and a tightening policy bias. The next leg of the rally will depend on whether corporate earnings support current valuations and the Nifty can clear resistance while holding its recently reclaimed support levels.

data.title: Kennedy, White House officials to revive food policy talks next week: Politico
data.description:
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is expected to meet with senior White House officials next week to discuss the status of U.S. food policy as part of a revived push to define ultra-processed foods, Politico reported on Saturday.

Discussions among officials have gathered pace over recent weeks after a pause this summer, according to three Trump administration officials who were granted anonymity to disclose internal conversations.

Previously, Kennedy promised to get a definition for ultra-processed foods “by April” and follow up with a system for food grading in a move that could tighten regulation on packaged offerings such as chips and sodas.

In August, the HHS and the U.S. Department of Agriculture submitted the federal government’s first proposed definition of ultra-processed foods for final review as a white paper, which, however, fell short of being a legally enforceable rule.

The discussions come less than two weeks into the midterm elections amid calls by Kennedy and many members of his Make America Healthy Again movement to include warning labels for ultra-processed foods.

HHS didn’t immediately respond to a request for comments.

Potentially relevant tickers: PepsiCo , Kellanova (K), Kraft Heinz , McDonald's , Yum! Brands , Restaurant Brands International , Coca-Cola , B&G Foods , Conagra Brands , Celsius , Hershey , Mondelez , and  Invesco Food & Beverage ETF

data.title: IDBI Bank Q2 profit falls 39% on high base, underlying earnings rise 14%
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 17 -- IDBI Bank reported a 39 per cent year-on-year decline in net profit to Rs 2,205 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, largely due to a one-time gain recorded last year, while its underlying profit grew 14 per cent amid stronger interest income and improving asset quality.

According to the bank's earnings release, net profit stood at Rs 3,627 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, which included a one-time gain of Rs 1,699 crore from the sale of its strategic investment in National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL).

The bank stated, "Excluding this one-off gain, YoY increase in Operating Profit and Net profit is 59% and 14% for Q2 FY27 respectively."

Operating profit stood at Rs 2,893 crore, compared with Rs 3,523 crore a year earlier. Excluding the exceptional gain, operating profit increased 59 per cent to Rs 1,824 crore.

The bank's core lending income also strengthened, with net interest income rising 29 per cent year-on-year to Rs 4,228 crore from Rs 3,285 crore.

Net interest margin improved to 4.11 per cent from 3.71 per cent a year earlier, while the cost of deposits declined to 4.55 per cent.

Asset quality also improved, with gross non-performing assets (NPAs) declining to 2.12 per cent from 2.65 per cent a year earlier, while net NPAs fell to 0.17 per cent from 0.21 per cent.

The bank stated, "The PCR is consistently above 99% since September 2023." Its provision coverage ratio, including technical write-offs, stood at 99.24 per cent.

Total deposits grew 17 per cent year-on-year to Rs 3.56 lakh crore, while net advances increased 18 per cent to Rs 2.72 lakh crore.

The results come amid the ongoing strategic disinvestment process in IDBI Bank, with the Finance Ministry issuing a clarification on Saturday concerning legislative developments related to the government's shareholding in the lender.

The latest earnings indicate stronger core banking performance and improving asset quality, despite the sharp decline in reported profit caused by last year's exceptional gain.

data.title: Bitcoin On Track For First Back-To-Back Losing Octobers In Over A Decade As ‘Downtober’ Continues
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bitcoin was down over 2% so far in October, putting it on track for its first back-to-back losing October in more than 10 years.
  • October has been one of Bitcoin's strongest months, averaging about 18% gains. 
  • Last year, Bitcoin hit its all-time high early in the month before an Oct. 10 crash sent it lower.

Bitcoin (BTC) was on track for its first consecutive October decline, with Bankless co-founder David Hoffman calling Friday “the third week of Downtober.”

October has long been one of Bitcoin's best months. Its average October return was about 18.3%, and its median is about 12.7%, according to CoinGlass data. Before last year, the month had ended lower only twice, in 2014 and 2018.

YearMonthly Returns In October
2026-2.48%
2025-3.69%
2024+10.76%
2023+28.52%
2022+5.56%
2021+39.93%
2020+27.7%
2019+10.17%
2018-3.83%
2017+47.81%
2016+14.71%

Source: Coinglass.

Last October started on a high. Bitcoin hit its all-time high of about $126,000 early in the month, before a crash on October 10 erased those gains. This year it has been different. The world's largest cryptocurrency was down over 2% so far this month. It also fell more than 3% last October. Bitcoin has not posted two red Octobers in a row in more than 10 years, with its highest gain in October being in 2017.

Bankless co-founders Hoffman and Ryan Sean Adams discussed that Bitcoin climbed into October from the $60,000s, rather than falling from a record. "The direction of travel is quite different," one of them said.

This Week's Slide

Bitcoin dipped to around $80,000 this week, its lowest level since September 18. It is down about 7% for the year. The selling had been heavier in altcoins, where Ethereum (ETH) fell about 7.5% over the week, the hosts said, while tokens like Solana (SOL), Zchas (ZEC), Hyperliquid (HYPE) and Near Protocol (NEAR) dropped another 10% after double-digit losses the week before.

'They Feel Sideways'

The hosts argued that a choppy market fits an early bull run. They pointed to 2023, when Bitcoin spent about seven months moving sideways and suffered two 17% pullbacks. Through that stretch, Bitcoin held above its 50-week moving average.

"So that's kind of the way early bull markets feel. They feel sideways," Adams said. Neither expected Bitcoin to fall below its low from a few months ago. "We have broken the back of the bear market," Adams added.

Bitcoin's monthly returns have swung widely this year. CoinGlass data showed it fell about 10% in January, 15% in February, and 20% in June, but gained about 25% in August.

data.title: Air India, Air India Express extend Saudi Arabia flight suspension until Oct 24 amid Houthi strikes: What airline said
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Air India and its subsidiary Air India Express have extended the suspension of services connecting Indian cities with Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam in Saudi Arabia until October 24, citing the prevailing security situation in West Asia following Houthi rebel strikes in the region.

The airline has also announced a one-time complimentary rescheduling facility for affected passengers, adding that tickets booked on or before October 15 for journeys scheduled between October 9 and 25 will be eligible for a free change of travel date, provided the revised journey takes place by November 10.

In a travel advisory, Air India said the extended suspension could disrupt passengers' travel arrangements and that the airlines were seeking to offer greater flexibility to those affected.

The statement read, "In view of the prevailing situation, Air India and Air India Express have temporarily suspended flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam until 24 October 2026. We understand that these disruptions may affect our guests' travel plans and are committed to providing as much flexibility as possible during this period."

"Guests holding confirmed Air India or Air India Express bookings issued on or before 15 October 2026, with travel dates between 9 October and 25 October 2026, are eligible for a one-time complimentary date change on their respective airline up to 10 November 2026. Guests who do not wish to rebook on the originally preferred sector for a future date may, instead, choose to rebook from an alternative station in the GCC region served by their respective airline, subject to availability," it added.

Affected passengers can also choose to travel to an alternative destination in West Asia, subject to the airline's applicable options. Air India customers can reschedule their journeys to or from Dubai or Doha, while Air India Express passengers can opt for Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Bahrain, Doha, Dubai, Kuwait, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Salalah or Sharjah, the airline said.

However, passengers will have to arrange their own transport to the alternative departure point and ensure they meet the relevant visa and entry requirements, it said, further stating that those whose flights have been cancelled can also opt for a full refund if they decide not to travel.

"We continue to closely monitor the situation and will keep guests informed of any further updates. Our priority remains to support affected guests, minimise inconvenience, and help them continue their journeys with suitable travel options," Air India concluded.

IndiGo on Thursday extended the suspension of its flights to Saudi Arabian destinations until October 24.

Akasa Air announced that it would continue to suspend services to and from Riyadh until October 24 and Jeddah until October 21, citing the prevailing security situation in the Middle East.

The flight disruptions follow the October 10 attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, which has claimed 13 lives. The death toll rose after the Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed that an Indian national, who was injured in the incident, succumbed to his injuries.

Meanwhile, amid the escalation of the conflict, Yemen's internationally recognised government on Friday accused Houthi rebels of launching two missiles targeting Aden International Airport. According to the country's Information Minister Moammar Al-Eryani, the missiles landed near a Yemenia Airways aircraft that was preparing to depart for Cairo.

data.title: Axis Bank's Q2 profit jumps 38% as provisions fall 52%, asset quality improves
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 17 -- Axis Bank reported a 38 per cent year-on-year jump in standalone net profit to Rs 7,003 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, supported by a sharp 52 per cent decline in provisions and improving asset quality, even as its core operating profit grew at a slower pace.

According to the bank's earnings release and investor presentation filed with the stock exchanges on Saturday, provisions and contingencies fell to Rs 1,694 crore from Rs 3,547 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The decline in provisions helped boost profitability despite operating profit rising only 6 per cent to Rs 11,083 crore.

However, the year-ago quarter included a one-time standard asset provision of Rs 1,231 crore, which contributed to the sharp year-on-year decline in provisions.

The bank stated in its investor presentation that "GNPA, NNPA, slippages and credit costs improved YOY and QOQ."

Gross non-performing assets (NPAs) declined to 1.16 per cent from 1.46 per cent a year earlier, while net NPAs improved to 0.35 per cent from 0.44 per cent.

Fresh loan slippages also fell to Rs 4,762 crore from Rs 5,696 crore in the year-ago quarter, indicating fewer loans turning bad.

The bank's annualised net credit cost declined to 0.45 per cent, down 28 basis points year-on-year.

Meanwhile, net interest income rose 12 per cent to Rs 15,371 crore, while net interest margin stood at 3.36 per cent.

The bank's earnings release highlighted "Robust growth in deposits at 21% YOY and 6% QOQ and advances at 23% YOY and 9% QOQ."

Total deposits reached Rs 14.52 lakh crore, while advances stood at Rs 13.74 lakh crore. Corporate lending grew 34 per cent year-on-year, outpacing retail loan growth of 16 per cent.

The results indicate that lower provisioning requirements and improving loan quality supported Axis Bank's earnings growth, alongside continued expansion in lending and deposits.

data.title: Deutsche Bank Nears Bitcoin Custody Launch As Crypto Push Expands Beyond Europe
data.description:
TL;DR: Deutsche Bank is preparing to introduce institutional digital asset custody services, initially targeting professional clients in Germany. The planned platform is part of a wider effort to connect cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets to established banking infrastructure.

Deutsche Bank is nearing the commercial launch of its institutional cryptocurrency custody business, another sign that major European lenders increasingly regard digital assets as part of mainstream financial services.

Comments reported on October 16 indicated that the German banking giant expects to begin serving institutional customers within weeks. Its offering is intended to support assets including Bitcoin and Ethereum, using technology developed with Swiss digital asset infrastructure company Taurus.

This is not a new retail cryptocurrency trading app. The initial market consists of businesses and professional investors with demanding custody and compliance requirements.

Why Banks Are Entering Custody

Holding cryptocurrency for institutional clients involves more than storing private keys. Banks must address asset segregation, operational controls, reporting, insurance arrangements and regulators’ expectations.

The service would allow eligible institutions to interact with digital assets through a familiar banking relationship rather than exclusively relying on specialised cryptocurrency companies.

Traditional finance is already developing related infrastructure. Projects involving blockchain settlement and tokenized deposits illustrate how established financial businesses are adapting their systems.

The Longer-Term Opportunity

Deutsche Bank has also discussed tokenized deposits, digital securities and possible expansion into Asian financial centres in 2027.

These ambitions remain subject to regulatory approvals and operating arrangements. A planned launch should not be confused with an already operating global service.

Nevertheless, the direction is clear. Rather than merely offering clients exposure to cryptocurrency prices, traditional banks increasingly want to provide the infrastructure through which digital assets are held, transferred and managed.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: HDFC Bank's Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha seeks to quit on December 31; details here
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- HDFC Bank's Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha has sought to step down from his role at the bank, effective December 31, 2026, the lender said in an exchange filing on Saturday.

"The GNRC and the Board of Directors, at their respective meetings held on October 16, 2026 and October 17, 2026, respected the decision of Mr. Bharucha and accepted his request to be forwarded to the Reserve Bank of India for approval," said the bank in its filing. (More to come)

data.title: Yes Bank Q2 Results: Low provisions, high other income aid profits; Asset quality stable
data.description:
Mumbai-based private lender Yes Bank Ltd. reported September quarter results on Saturday, October 17, which were higher on a year-on-year basis on the profitability and core income front.

Yes Bank's Net Interest Income (NII) or core income that it earned, grew by 22.7% during the quarter to ₹2,822.5 crore, compared to ₹2,301 crore it reported during the same quarter last year.

Net profit for the period stood at ₹1,080 crore. That's a 65% growth compared to the year-ago period and also means that the bank has not taken into account any potential losses arising from the AT-1 bond issue, which led to the stock declining nearly 20% across Thursday and Friday.

Asset quality for the private lender remained stable with Gross NPA at 1.2% from 1.3% in June, while Net NPA remaining unchanged at 0.2% from 0.2% in the previous quarter. In absolute terms, Yes Bank's Gross NPA stood at ₹3,875 crore, while its Net NPA stood at ₹757 crore. This is in comparison to the ₹3,704 crore and ₹677 crore it reported respectively during the previous quarter.

Provisions for the quarter declined to ₹317.4 crore from ₹395 crore in June, while other income increased to ₹1,881.5 crore from ₹1,644.3 crore last year. Both contributed to the growth in the bank's profitability.

Based on its business update reported earlier this month, Yes Bank's loans and advances had grown by 23.8% on a year-on-year basis to ₹3.09 lakh crore, while deposits saw growth of 19.5% to ₹3.54 lakh crore from ₹2.96 lakh crore earlier.

CASA Ratio stood at 33.7% from 30% in the year-ago period. Normalized for the FCNR (B) inflows, Yes Bank's loan growth stood at 17.7% and deposit growth stood at 13.2% from last year.

Yes Bank has been in the news through Thursday and Friday after the Supreme Court decided to set aside the write-off of its Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds worth over ₹8,400 crore.

Sources had told CNBC-TV18 exclusively that the lender could recognize the potential ₹5,300 crore to ₹5,400 crore earnings hit during the ongoing quarter itself, or push it to the December quarter, but not later than that.

The write-off had taken place during the RBI-led reconstruction of Yes Bank, when the lender was facing a severe financial crisis. The rescue involved capital support from State Bank of India and other lenders, while the AT-1 bonds were written down to zero.

Shares of Yes Bank had ended at the day's low on Friday as well, declining 3.4% to end at ₹17.5. This follows a 14.5% drop on Thursday after the Supreme Court judgment.
